title: Propositional compactness: infinite constraints and finite proofs
summary: Finite satisfiability gives one valuation for an arbitrary theory, and every consequence has a finite proof.
abstract: An infinite list of propositional requirements asks for one truth assignment that meets them all. If every finite selection can be met, must the whole list have a solution? Compactness answers yes for ordinary finite formulas, even when the set of atoms is uncountable. It also shows that any conclusion forced by all the requirements is already forced by finitely many of them. Combining this with finite-premise completeness gives a finite natural-deduction proof of every such conclusion. Thus a theory has no proof of a contradiction exactly when all its formulas can be made true together.
